name: DirectX Shader Compiler (dxcompiler.dll)
use: Unchanged Microsoft-signed runtime binary shipped beside the Windows Cycles host. The shipped CodeBrix.WebGpu.Native runtime loads it (WGPUInstanceExtras.dxcPath) to compile the WGSL kernels' HLSL for Direct3D 12. Not a build input: no source is compiled against it.
why: Measured on the win-x64 development machine (integrated Intel GPU, CodeBrix.WebGpu.Native 1.0.290.1433) by compiling every compute entry point of five real Cycles WGSL modules (32 pipelines; native/evidence/merge-20261023c/wgsl-modules: two surface, one shadow and one background module plus the largest, 457,744 bytes). D3D12 with DXC: 32 of 32 pipelines compiled. Vulkan (reference): 32 of 32. D3D12 with FXC (d3dcompiler_47.dll, part of Windows): failed shade_background and shader_eval_background (Internal error: FXC D3DCompile error 0x80004005) and prepare_surface of the largest module, and needed 252 s for a prepare_shader_data pipeline that DXC compiled in 8 s and Vulkan in 4 s. FXC therefore cannot be the Windows compiler; wgpu.h names DXC v1.8.2502 as the minimum supported version.

license.note: The release zip and the NuGet package also carry LICENSE-MS.txt (Microsoft Software License Terms, DirectX Shader Compiler), which historically applied to dxil.dll and which the current ReleaseNotes mapping does not assign to any file. Its terms (distributor indemnity, downstream terms) are not compatible with an Apache-2.0-only release. No file it could cover is imported: dxil.dll is excluded, and since DXC v1.8.2505 the compiler always uses its internal validator instead of an external dxil.dll (ReleaseNotes).
